counting_contract.working: The 53 current records are 45 registered criteria plus 8 unregistered proposals; historical/inactive versions are excluded.
counting_contract.execution: 31 exact rule/attribute versions admitted to rules@v1, including 13 exploratory context entries.
counting_contract.independent_core: Only preference and hard_exclusion entries; exact quantity_identity plus exact decision semantics, without merging similar names or different assay conditions.
counting_contract.quantity: Use explicit quantity_id with units and mathematical transform when present; otherwise use the existing evidence route identity. No enabled entry declares an explicit quantity_id in this freeze.
counting_contract.decision: Quantity identity plus measurement_kind, aggregation and aggregation_scope, rule_kind, predicate_form, cutoff, direction, on_missing/on_conflict/on_inapplicable.
counting_contract.context: exploratory_consideration entries are retained for context and assessed records; they are not ranking preferences or qualification gates.
counting_contract.pending: The 5 review-pending registered refs are a subset of the 14 deferred entries; the 8 unregistered proposals are a separate population. These counts must not be added twice.
counting_contract.limit: Exact contract-based groups are reported, not an asserted universal count of semantically unique scientific concepts. Distinct route/method identities are not collapsed by name.
counting_contract.reason_origin: Deferred reasons come from the immutable frozen rule_set; unregistered reasons and validation findings come from their latest stored proposal and cached change record, verified against source artifacts.

enabled.name: Food effect on AUC (fold-change)
enabled.definition: Fold-change in AUC due to food effect on oral absorption, as reported in clinical pharmacology studies or labels. A value of 1 indicates no food effect; values greater than 1 indicate increased exposure with food.

parameters.query_template: ({names}) AND ("food effect" OR "fasted" OR "fed") AND (pharmacokinetics OR absorption)

enabled.rationale: Food effects can significantly alter oral exposure and complicate dosing. A smaller fold-change (closer to 1) is preferred for clinical development. The cited claims report food effects for specific agents, but no universal cutoff is stated, so this remains an exploratory consideration.

enabled.name: Molecular weight (Da)
enabled.definition: Molecular weight of the compound in Daltons (g/mol), computed from structure by the curated descriptor route rather than a trained prediction; lower values are preferred because size above roughly 500 Da approaches the upper limit compatible with efficient passive intestinal diffusion and increases efflux-transporter recognition.

enabled.name: Oral bioavailability (human, measured F%)
enabled.definition: Reported absolute or relative oral bioavailability (F%) in humans, as a measured pharmacokinetic parameter. Higher values indicate greater fraction of an orally administered dose reaching systemic circulation intact. This is a preference ordering, not a requirement: low F% compounds may still be clinically effective if the dose can be escalated.
enabled.rationale: Directly measures the fraction of an oral dose reaching systemic circulation in humans. The objective requires oral administration; a measured human F% is a decision-relevant absorption parameter. Multiple claims report human F% values (e.g., 58%, 38-49%, 85-90%, 21.4%, 4.7%, 69-83%, 25%). No claim states a required minimum F%, so the rule ranks by value without a cutoff. The ordering is a preference, not a requirement: low F% compounds may still be clinically effective if the dose can be escalated.

enabled.name: Predicted aqueous solubility (log mol/L)
enabled.definition: Model-predicted aqueous solubility in log(mol/L) from the ADMET-AI Solubility_AqSolDB model; recorded as a descriptive consideration because the cited claims report solubility as a generic drug-like property and give low-solubility examples, without validating this endpoint or establishing a direction for this library.

enabled.name: Predicted blood-brain barrier penetration probability (BBB_Martins)
enabled.definition: Model-predicted probability of blood-brain barrier penetration; lower probability is generally preferred for peripheral targets to minimise CNS side effects.
enabled.rationale: BBB penetration can lead to CNS side effects; for oncology targets outside the CNS, lower penetration is often preferred. The model's held-out AUROC is 0.9004, supporting its use as a preference.

enabled.name: Predicted BRENK alert count
enabled.definition: Number of BRENK alerts from RDKit; higher counts indicate greater likelihood of problematic substructures.
enabled.rationale: BRENK alerts flag substructures associated with toxicity or poor pharmacokinetics. The ADMET-AI BRENK_alert endpoint provides a count for every compound with a structure. This is a deterministic RDKit calculation.

enabled.name: Predicted Caco-2 permeability (ADMET-AI Caco2_Wang, log 10^-6 cm/s)
enabled.definition: Model-predicted apparent permeability coefficient across Caco-2 monolayers from the ADMET-AI Caco2_Wang endpoint, in log(10^-6 cm/s); recorded as a descriptive consideration because the cited claims report low permeability for specific poorly absorbed compounds without validating this endpoint or establishing a direction for this library.

enabled.name: Predicted clinical toxicity probability (exploratory)
enabled.definition: ADMET-AI ClinTox model output: predicted probability in [0,1] of clinical toxicity. The catalog documents the endpoint, its unit and its direction (higher probability is worse). Recorded as an exploratory consideration only: the cited evidence documents general toxicity and dose-limiting adverse events for this drug class but no cited claim validates this model or states a probability threshold. Where several predicted values are available for a compound, the worst-case (maximum) value is recorded.

enabled.name: Predicted CYP1A2 inhibition probability
enabled.definition: Model-predicted probability that the compound inhibits CYP1A2, in [0,1]; higher values indicate greater drug-drug interaction liability.
enabled.rationale: CYP1A2 inhibition can alter the metabolism of co-administered drugs. The ADMET-AI CYP1A2_Veith endpoint provides a predicted probability for every compound with a structure. The model's held-out AUROC is 0.9411, supporting a preference rule.

enabled.name: Predicted CYP2C19 inhibition probability
enabled.definition: Model-predicted probability that the compound inhibits CYP2C19, in [0,1]; higher values indicate greater drug-drug interaction liability.
enabled.rationale: CYP2C19 inhibition can alter the metabolism of co-administered drugs. The ADMET-AI CYP2C19_Veith endpoint provides a predicted probability for every compound with a structure. The model's held-out AUROC is 0.9062, supporting a preference rule.

enabled.name: Predicted CYP2C9 inhibition probability
enabled.definition: Model-predicted probability that the compound inhibits CYP2C9, in [0,1]; higher values indicate greater drug-drug interaction liability.
enabled.rationale: CYP2C9 inhibition is a common source of drug-drug interactions. The ADMET-AI CYP2C9_Veith endpoint provides a predicted probability for every compound with a structure. The model's held-out AUROC is 0.9077, supporting a preference rule.

enabled.name: Predicted CYP2C9 substrate probability
enabled.definition: Model-predicted probability that the compound is a CYP2C9 substrate, in [0,1]; higher values indicate greater susceptibility to CYP2C9-mediated metabolism and potential drug-drug interactions.
enabled.rationale: Being a CYP2C9 substrate increases the risk of metabolic drug-drug interactions. The ADMET-AI CYP2C9_Substrate_CarbonMangels endpoint provides a predicted probability for every compound with a structure. The model's held-out AUROC is 0.6279, so this is an auxiliary preference.

enabled.name: Predicted CYP3A4 inhibition probability (exploratory)
enabled.definition: ADMET-AI CYP3A4_Veith model output: predicted probability in [0,1] that the compound inhibits CYP3A4, i.e. acts as a perpetrator of CYP3A4-mediated drug-drug interactions. The catalog documents the endpoint, its unit and its direction (higher probability is worse). Recorded as an exploratory consideration only: the cited evidence documents CYP3A4-mediated drug-drug interaction liability for this drug class but no cited claim validates this model or states a probability threshold.

enabled.name: Predicted CYP3A4 substrate probability (exploratory)
enabled.definition: ADMET-AI CYP3A4_Substrate_CarbonMangels model output: predicted probability in [0,1] that the compound is a substrate of CYP3A4, i.e. is susceptible to CYP3A4-mediated metabolism and to victim-side drug-drug interactions. The catalog documents the endpoint, its unit and its direction (higher probability is worse). Recorded as an exploratory consideration only: the cited evidence documents CYP3A4 substrate liability for this drug class but no cited claim validates this model or states a probability threshold.

enabled.name: Predicted drug-induced liver injury (DILI) probability (exploratory)
enabled.definition: ADMET-AI DILI model output: predicted probability in [0,1] that the compound causes drug-induced liver injury. The catalog documents the endpoint, its unit and its direction (higher probability is worse). Recorded as an exploratory consideration only: the cited evidence documents hepatotoxicity as a frequent, dose-limiting liability of this drug class but no cited claim validates this model or states a probability threshold. Where several predicted values are available for a compound, the worst-case (maximum) value is recorded.

enabled.name: Predicted hERG blocking probability (exploratory)
enabled.definition: ADMET-AI hERG classifier output: predicted probability in [0,1] that a compound blocks the hERG potassium channel, the mechanistic driver of QT prolongation and torsades de pointes liability during chronic oral dosing. The catalog documents the endpoint, its unit and its direction (higher probability is worse). Recorded as an exploratory consideration only: the cited evidence documents QT-prolongation events for kinase inhibitors and asserts off-target hERG inhibition for a drug class, but no cited claim validates this model or states a probability threshold. Where several predicted values are available for a compound, the worst-case (maximum) value is recorded.

enabled.name: Predicted human hepatocyte intrinsic clearance (exploratory)
enabled.definition: ADMET-AI Clearance_Hepatocyte_AZ model output: predicted human hepatocyte intrinsic clearance in uL/min/10^6 cells. The catalog documents the endpoint, its unit and its direction (higher clearance is worse). Recorded as an exploratory consideration only: the cited evidence establishes that metabolic stability is a development criterion and reports measured hepatocyte clearance values that fix the direction, but no cited claim validates this model or states a numeric threshold. Where several predicted values are available for a compound, the median is recorded.

enabled.name: Predicted logP (RDKit)
enabled.definition: Model-predicted logP (RDKit); lower values are preferred because lipophilic, poorly soluble agents show food-dependent and variable oral absorption.
enabled.rationale: The cited claim reports that lipophilic, poorly soluble agents have food-dependent absorption, supporting lower lipophilicity as a preference for consistent oral exposure. No cutoff is asserted because the claim states no logP number.

enabled.name: Predicted microsomal intrinsic clearance (exploratory)
enabled.definition: ADMET-AI Clearance_Microsome_AZ model output: predicted human liver microsomal intrinsic clearance in uL/min/mg. The catalog documents the endpoint, its unit and its direction (higher clearance is worse). Recorded as an exploratory consideration only: the cited evidence establishes that metabolic stability is a development criterion and reports measured clearance values that fix the direction, but no cited claim validates this model or states a numeric threshold. Where several predicted values are available for a compound, the median is recorded.

enabled.name: Predicted NIH alert count
enabled.definition: Number of NIH alerts from RDKit; higher counts indicate greater likelihood of problematic substructures.
enabled.rationale: NIH alerts flag substructures associated with toxicity or poor pharmacokinetics. The ADMET-AI NIH_alert endpoint provides a count for every compound with a structure. This is a deterministic RDKit calculation.

enabled.name: Predicted PAINS alert count
enabled.definition: Number of PAINS alerts from RDKit; higher counts indicate greater likelihood of assay interference and poor drug-likeness.
enabled.rationale: PAINS alerts flag compounds prone to assay interference, which can undermine development. The ADMET-AI PAINS_alert endpoint provides a count for every compound with a structure. This is a deterministic RDKit calculation, so it is reliable.

enabled.name: Predicted plasma protein binding rate (ADMET-AI PPBR_AZ, %)
enabled.definition: Model-predicted percentage of compound bound to plasma proteins from the ADMET-AI PPBR_AZ endpoint; recorded as a descriptive consideration because the cited claims report that high protein binding can reduce free drug concentration and give PPB distributions, without validating this endpoint or establishing a direction for this library.

enabled.name: Predicted skin reaction probability (exploratory)
enabled.definition: ADMET-AI Skin_Reaction model output: predicted probability in [0,1] that a compound elicits a skin reaction (rash, hand-foot skin reaction). The catalog documents the endpoint, its unit and its direction (higher probability is worse). Recorded as an exploratory consideration only: the cited evidence documents that dermatologic toxicity is a frequent, dose-limiting class liability of chronically dosed oral kinase inhibitors, but no cited claim validates this model or states a probability threshold. Where several predicted values are available for a compound, the worst-case (maximum) value is recorded.

enabled.name: Predicted volume of distribution at steady state
enabled.definition: Model-predicted volume of distribution (L/kg); affects tissue distribution and potential for toxicity.
enabled.rationale: Volume of distribution influences tissue exposure and toxicity. The VDss_Lombardo model has negative R2 (-1.2107), meaning it does not beat the mean; therefore, this attribute is exploratory only and should not carry a cutoff.

enabled.name: Time to maximum plasma concentration (Tmax, median of reported values)
enabled.definition: Median of reported times to maximum plasma concentration after oral administration, in hours; when a source reports only a range, the range midpoint is used. Lower values indicate faster absorption. This is a preference ordering, not a requirement: longer Tmax may still be compatible with oral bioavailability and efficacy.
enabled.rationale: Tmax is a direct measure of oral absorption rate. Cited claims report measured Tmax values of 4 h and 3 h and ranges of 1-4 h, 2-4 h, 3-4 h and 6-12 h for orally administered agents, establishing the quantity as measurable and decision-relevant, but no claim states a required Tmax, so the rule ranks by value without a cutoff. The ordering is a preference, not a requirement: longer Tmax may still be compatible with oral bioavailability and efficacy.
